summary: Conclusion: **real, public Neyriz geochemical measurements do exist**, principally as publisher-hosted supplementary spreadsheets and an open article table. However, neither verified public source supplies sample latitude/longitude, an AOI polygon, or CRS. Thus they are reproducibly usable as tabular geochemical/reference data, but **not directly usable as spatial geochemical point layers or as the geochemistry-evidence layer in a reproducible GIS prospectivity model**. The main verified dataset is Stern et al.'s public Taylor & Francis Figshare record (DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.1132662.v1): six files, all downloaded individually and MD5-verified against the publisher API. It includes mineral chemistry, clinopyroxene trace/REE, whole-rock major/trace/REE, Sr-Nd-Pb isotope data, and methods. Coverage is described only as the Neyriz ophiolite, southern Iran/northeast flank of the Zagros fold-thrust belt; all inspected spreadsheets and the methods DOCX lack coordinate fields, so CRS is absent/not applicable. Publicly readable Attarzadeh et al. (2017) also provides 16 chromitite analyses from eastern Neyriz (Dowlat Abad–Tang-e Hana), but no sample coordinates/CRS in the actual accessible text/PDF table. **Public data:** the Figshare supplements (CC BY 4.0) and the SCIRP table/article (CC BY 4.0). **Authenticated/request-only or unverified candidates:** GEOROC's API documentation requires a provider-issued API key; no Neyriz query/download was verified without one. The official NGDIR/GSI endpoints were unreachable from this environment, so no official Iranian downloadable dataset, login rule, licence, or formal-request pathway can be claimed. **Field/lab work:** not necessary to reuse the published numeric values, but new field sampling/laboratory assays, author-provided coordinates, or a formally obtained official survey dataset would be required to build a defensible georeferenced geochemistry layer. Do not geocode sample IDs or infer coordinates from the regional descriptions. Exact Figshare public endpoints: https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/1628043 , /1628044 , /1628045 , /1628046 , /1628047 , /1628048; archive endpoint https://tandf.figshare.com/ndownloader/articles/1132662/versions/1 is also published but returned an AWS WAF challenge in this environment, whereas each individual file endpoint worked.

sources.title: Taylor & Francis Figshare — Supra-subduction zone magmatism of the Neyriz ophiolite, Iran: constraints from geochemistry and Sr-Nd-Pb isotopes
sources.status: Verified public publisher-hosted dataset; record read and all six individual files downloaded and checksum-verified.
sources.notes: DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.1132662.v1; posted 2014-08-08, modified 2023-05-30; public, no embargo, CC BY 4.0. Coverage metadata is narrative only: Neyriz ophiolite, southern Iran/northeast Zagros; no bounding coordinates or sample-coordinate table. CRS: none supplied because all inspected supplement tables lack latitude, longitude, UTM, easting, northing, or coordinate fields. Actual downloadable endpoints: https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/1628043 (Table 5 Sr-Nd-Pb isotopes, XLS, 38,400 B); https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/1628044 (Table 4 whole-rock gabbro/dike/lava major, trace and REE, XLSX, 27,167 B); https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/1628045 (Table 3 whole-rock peridotite/gabbro major, trace and REE, XLS, 62,976 B); https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/1628046 (Table 2 clinopyroxene trace/REE, XLS, 48,128 B); https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/1628047 (Table 1 mineral chemistry, XLS, 353,280 B); https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/1628048 (analytical methods, DOCX, 19,503 B). The data can be converted reproducibly to tidy non-spatial tables, but cannot become GIS sample points without independently sourced/author-supplied locations.

sources.title: Figshare public REST record for article 1132662
sources.notes: The API exposes file names, sizes, MIME types, exact direct download URLs, MD5 checksums, public status, DOI, dates and CC BY 4.0 licence. Downloaded file MD5 values matched the six API checksums: 162ad2327f20c39e77e5019854e0b618; d005899975f46aece57ec0a62d91be58; d566e04bd34df071540c3199170fd2bd; 1b89e48068f1583906177874df66ddc8; 0fffb2ab83d4273df9b5e1ad7da08478; 2f2126fac1252ee5378c0100b5b2d18f. This is the reproducible discovery/download endpoint, not a spatial API.

sources.title: Attarzadeh et al. (2017), Geochemistry of Chromitites in Eastern Part of Neyriz Ophiolite Complex (Southern Iran)
sources.status: Verified public full text; its linked PDF endpoint was also opened/read.
sources.notes: Published 2017-03-14; CC BY 4.0. Exact PDF/download endpoint: http://www.scirp.org/journal/PaperDownload.aspx?paperID=74691 . The actual Table 1 lists 16 samples (D.T.1–D.T.16) from the eastern Neyriz Dowlat Abad–Tang-e Hana area, with SiO2, Al2O3, CaO, Fe2O3, FeO, K2O, MgO, MnO, Na2O, P2O5, TiO2 and Cr2O3 in wt%; XRF methods and laboratory are stated. Study coverage is a named subarea, not a machine-readable AOI. No sample lat/long/UTM/CRS was found in the accessible article/PDF table. It is usable as openly licensed tabular chemistry; GIS use would require independently documented sample locations, not inferred placement.

sources.title: GEOROC Database — Georg-August-Universität Göttingen official description
sources.status: Authoritative candidate database, but no Neyriz-specific record or download was verified in this research.
sources.notes: The official page states GEOROC provides free access to >30 million geochemical values and that its metadata include latitude/longitude, analytical methods, laboratory and references—potentially suitable for GIS if a Neyriz result is retrieved. The public query page opened at https://georoc.eu/georoc/new-start.asp, but no actual Neyriz result was produced. The provider’s published notebook states that API access requires a provider-issued API key and points to https://api-test.georoc.eu/api/v1/docs/index.html#/ . Therefore do not claim a Neyriz download, endpoint response, licence, CRS, dates or coverage until a query with authorised access returns a citable record. API-key/authentication requirement is distinct from field/lab work.

sources.title: National Geoscience Database of Iran (NGDIR) official portal
sources.status: Official national candidate source, but inaccessible from the assigned environment; no metadata or download was verified.
sources.notes: Direct HTTPS browsing returned connection-closed/SSL errors and HTTP returned an empty reply; no portal content, catalogue, data endpoint, licence, login requirement, request procedure, CRS, date or Neyriz coverage could be read. This is not evidence that NGDIR/GSI data do not exist; it is a strict access/verification blocker. Any use of a national geochemical survey must be obtained through an official documented download or formal request and accompanied by its actual licence, survey date, analytical method, coordinate reference system and sample-location metadata.

sources.title: EarthChem terms and data-access overview
sources.status: Authoritative global-data access reference; not a verified Neyriz dataset result.
sources.notes: EarthChem offers PetDB and EarthChem Portal search interfaces, but no Neyriz AOI query/download was verified here. Its terms at https://earthchem.org/legal/terms-of-use/ state that digital materials carry varying Creative Commons licences and require adequate citation; dataset-specific licence must be checked on a result landing page. It is therefore a possible follow-up discovery route, not currently evidence of usable Neyriz data.

blockers: No coordinates, coordinate reference system, AOI polygon or spatial sample metadata in either verified public Neyriz chemistry source; a reproducible GIS point layer cannot be created from them alone.
The official NGDIR portal and GSI host could not be accessed from this sandbox; no official Neyriz survey file/API/request rules could be verified and none should be invented.
GEOROC's published API workflow requires a provider-issued API key; no authenticated Neyriz search was performed, so the existence of a GEOROC Neyriz record remains unverified.
The Figshare all-files archive endpoint was WAF-challenged here, but this did not block the verified public individual file endpoints listed above.
